# Diagnostics reference

Every problem `typed_openapi` finds in a spec, an overrides file, a baseline or a config has a stable code such as `TOA501`. This guide is the single reference for all 135 codes: what each one means and how to fix it. It is generated from the doc comments of the `DiagnosticCode` enum, so it cannot drift from the tool. Other guides link here instead of repeating the table.

```text
warning TOA501 missing-path-parameter: The path /products/{id} has {id}, but this operation declares no path parameter "id"; it is added as a required string path parameter.
  --> specs/shop.yaml:30:7
  at #/paths/~1products~1{id}/get
  fix: Declare each at the source as {name: <name>, in: path, required: true, schema: {type: string}}.
```

A code never changes meaning once released. The slug (`missing-path-parameter`) is its readable name; both work wherever a code is accepted.

## Severity and levels

Every code has a default severity: `error`, `warning` or `info`. Errors make `check` and `generate` exit with `1`; warnings and infos do not (see [CLI](cli.md#exit-codes)). A client changes the level of a code in `severity:` of the config, by id or by slug, and `off` removes the code from the report (see [Configuration](configuration.md#severity)).

```yaml
clients:
  shop:
    input: specs/shop.yaml
    output: lib/src/api/shop
    severity:
      TOA201: info
      duplicate-operation-id: error
      TOA553: off
```

Three groups of codes are limited:

| Group | Codes | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Config codes | TOA901, TOA902, TOA903, TOA904 | The level cannot be changed at all, because the config is read before levels apply. Setting one is TOA902. Marked `config` below. |
| Fixed codes | Marked `fixed` below | The level can be raised but not lowered, and they cannot be turned off. |
| Everything else | All other codes | Any of `error`, `warning`, `info`, `off`. |

> **Note:** A baseline accepts only errors and warnings of codes that are not fixed. Infos are never accepted. See [Baseline](baseline.md).

The "Default" column is the severity before `severity:` applies.

> **Gotcha:** Two diagnostics that are equal (same code, severity, message, file, pointer and start position) are reported once, so a region of the spec that is read twice does not repeat its problems.

### TOA001 `parse-error`

Default: error (fixed).

The document is not valid JSON or YAML.

**Example.** A YAML file with a tab in its indentation, or a JSON file with a trailing comma.

**Fix.** Correct the syntax at the source; the message gives the line and column.

### TOA002 `duplicate-key`

Default: warning.

A mapping repeats a key.

**Example.** Two `get:` keys under one path item.

**Fix.** Remove one of the keys.

### TOA003 `root-not-object`

Default: error (fixed).

The document root is not an object.

**Example.** A file whose top level is a list or a string.

**Fix.** Make the top level of the file an OpenAPI object.

### TOA004 `input-not-found`

Default: error (fixed).

The input file, or a file a `$ref` points to, does not exist.

**Example.** `input:` in the config names a file that is not there, or a `$ref` points to a missing file.

**Fix.** Check `input` in the config, or download a fresh snapshot of the spec.

### TOA005 `positions-unavailable`

Default: info.

Source positions could not be recorded for a document.

**Example.** A `.json` file that the position-tracking reader rejects but plain JSON decoding accepts.

**Fix.** Nothing to do; the diagnostics of that file show JSON pointers and no line.

### TOA006 `input-unreadable`

Default: error (fixed).

The input file exists but cannot be read as UTF-8 text.

**Example.** `input:` points at a directory, or at a file that is not UTF-8 text or cannot be opened.

**Fix.** Point `input` at the spec file itself if it is a directory; otherwise save the spec as UTF-8 and check the file permissions.

### TOA007 `nesting-too-deep`

Default: error (fixed).

The document nests deeper than the parser can follow, in its text or once YAML aliases are expanded.

**Example.** A JSON file with more than 1000 nested arrays.

**Fix.** Flatten the document at the source.

### TOA008 `alias-expansion-too-large`

Default: error (fixed).

YAML aliases expand to far more nodes than the text has, or the JSON pointers of the document's nodes add up to more than the budget.

**Example.** A chain of YAML anchors in which each one aliases the previous anchor several times, so that a short file expands to millions of nodes.

**Fix.** Write the repeated part out once and refer to it with `$ref` instead of YAML aliases.

### TOA009 `yaml-tag-unsupported`

Default: error.

A YAML tag outside the JSON Schema ruleset OpenAPI requires, such as `!!timestamp` or `!custom`; the value is read as its text.

**Example.** A value written as `!!timestamp 2001-12-14` or `!custom x`.

**Fix.** Remove the tag, or quote the value so that it is a plain string.

### TOA010 `missing-openapi-version`

Default: error (fixed).

The document has no `openapi` field.

**Example.** A document that starts with `info:` and has no `openapi:` line.

**Fix.** Add the version the backend emits, for example `openapi: 3.0.3`.

### TOA011 `unsupported-openapi-version`

Default: error (fixed).

The document declares a version this tool does not read.

**Example.** A Swagger 2.0 document (`swagger: "2.0"`) or `openapi: 4.0.0`.

**Fix.** Have the backend emit OpenAPI 3, or convert the document.

### TOA012 `unknown-openapi-minor-version`

Default: warning.

The document declares a 3.x minor version newer than 3.2.

**Example.** `openapi: 3.3.0`.

**Fix.** Declare `openapi: 3.2.0` if the document is written to that version.

### TOA013 `openapi-version-not-string`

Default: warning.

The `openapi` field is not a string, so YAML may have changed it (3.10 reads as 3.1).

**Example.** `openapi: 3.10` in YAML, which a YAML parser reads as the number 3.1.

**Fix.** Quote the version, for example `openapi: "3.1.0"`.

### TOA015 `yaml-warning`

Default: warning.

The YAML parser warns about the text, for example about an unknown directive; reading goes on.

**Example.** A YAML directive that the parser does not know.

**Fix.** Fix the construct the message names, or remove it.

### TOA020 `openapi-3-1-in-3-0`

Default: warning.

A 3.0 document uses an OpenAPI 3.1 or JSON Schema 2020-12 construct; it is read as 3.1.

**Example.** `openapi: 3.0.3` with a schema that has `type: [string, "null"]` or `const`.

**Fix.** Declare `openapi: 3.1.0` if the backend emits 3.1; otherwise remove the construct.

### TOA021 `nullable-after-3-0`

Default: warning.

A 3.1 or later document uses `nullable`, which only 3.0 defines; it is read as in 3.0.

**Example.** `openapi: 3.1.0` with a schema that has `nullable: true`.

**Fix.** Write `type: [<type>, "null"]` instead of `nullable: true`.

### TOA022 `openapi-3-2-in-older`

Default: info.

A document older than 3.2 uses an OpenAPI 3.2 construct; it is read anyway.

**Example.** `openapi: 3.1.0` with an `in: querystring` parameter or an `itemSchema`.

**Fix.** Declare `openapi: 3.2.0` if the backend emits 3.2; otherwise remove the construct.

### TOA100 `invalid-ref`

Default: error.

A `$ref` is empty, truncated or not a URI with a JSON pointer.

**Example.** `$ref: ''` or a `$ref` with a query string such as `a.yaml?x=1`.

**Fix.** Fix the code that writes the spec; in NestJS this usually means a circular import made a DTO type undefined.

### TOA101 `unresolved-ref`

Default: error.

A `$ref` points to a file or a node that does not exist.

**Example.** `$ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'` when `components.schemas` has no `Pet`.

**Fix.** Define the target, or point the reference at an existing one.

### TOA102 `remote-ref`

Default: error.

A `$ref` points to a remote URL; only local files are read.

**Example.** `$ref: 'https://example.com/common.yaml#/Error'`.

**Fix.** Save the document next to the spec and refer to it by a relative path.

### TOA103 `ref-cycle`

Default: error.

`$ref`s point at each other in a loop that never reaches a definition.

**Example.** `A: {$ref: B}` and `B: {$ref: A}`.

**Fix.** Point one of them at the actual definition.

### TOA104 `ref-kind-mismatch`

Default: error.

A `$ref` points to a node of another kind, such as a schema where a parameter is expected.

**Example.** A `$ref` in a `parameters` list that points to a schema.

**Fix.** Point the `$ref` at a node of the kind the place expects.

### TOA105 `ref-base-ignored`

Default: warning.

`$id` or `$self` would change the base URI of `$ref`s; this tool resolves them against the file location instead.

**Example.** A schema with `$id: https://example.com/schemas/pet` whose `$ref`s are relative.

**Fix.** Remove `$id` or `$self` if it only names the schema; references are resolved against the file.

### TOA106 `invalid-component-key`

Default: warning.

A key in `components` has characters OpenAPI does not allow there.

**Example.** A key such as `Pet Store` under `components.schemas`; OpenAPI allows letters, digits and `.`, `-`, `_`.

**Fix.** Rename it at the source; type names are derived from it.

### TOA107 `ref-not-allowed`

Default: warning.

A `$ref` where OpenAPI does not accept a Reference Object, as bundlers such as Redocly allow; it is ignored.

**Example.** A `$ref` beside the `get:` key of a path item, or in place of the `info` object.

**Fix.** Write the object in place, or use a bundler to inline the reference.

### TOA108 `ref-commented-out`

Default: warning.

`$ref: #/...` without quotes in YAML: `#` starts a comment, so the value is null.

**Example.** `$ref: #/components/schemas/Pet` without quotes in YAML.

**Fix.** Quote the reference: `$ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'`.

### TOA109 `yaml-merge-key`

Default: warning.

A YAML 1.1 merge key `<<`, which OpenAPI's YAML does not have; it is read as a plain key named `<<`.

**Example.** A mapping with `<<: *defaults`.

**Fix.** Write the keys out.

### TOA110 `unknown-key`

Default: warning.

An object has a key that no OpenAPI version defines; it is ignored.

**Example.** A schema with `nullabel: true`, or a key that no OpenAPI version has and that does not start with `x-`.

**Fix.** Fix the spelling, or prefix a custom key with `x-`.

### TOA111 `invalid-value`

Default: warning.

A field has the wrong JSON type or a value the spec does not allow; it is ignored.

**Example.** `type: strng` on a schema, or `required: yes` where a list is expected.

**Fix.** For an unknown `type`, use one of `string`, `number`, `integer`, `boolean`, `array`, `object`, `null`; otherwise give the field the type the message names.

### TOA112 `missing-required-field`

Default: warning.

A field the spec requires is missing.

**Example.** An `info` object without `title`, or a parameter without `name`.

**Fix.** Add the field the message names at the source.

### TOA113 `non-string-key`

Default: error.

A mapping key is a collection, or an alias of one, instead of a string; the entry is ignored.

**Example.** A YAML key written as `? [a, b]`.

**Fix.** Write the key as a plain or quoted string.

### TOA114 `null-key`

Default: warning.

A mapping key is a YAML null (`~`, `null` or empty); it is read as its text.

**Example.** A YAML key written as `~:` or `null:`, or an empty key.

**Fix.** Quote the key, for example `"null":`.

## Normalizer and schema mapping (TOA2xx)

Schema problems that the normalizer repairs or the mapper has to work around.

| [TOA253](#toa253-allof-part-ignored) | `allof-part-ignored` | warning |
| [TOA254](#toa254-excluded-schema-referenced) | `excluded-schema-referenced` | info |
| [TOA255](#toa255-oneof-constraints-ignored) | `oneof-constraints-ignored` | info |
| [TOA256](#toa256-composition-parts-ignored) | `composition-parts-ignored` | warning |

### TOA201 `bool-required`

Default: warning.

A property schema says `required: true` or `false` (OpenAPI 2 style); for `true` the name is moved into the object's `required` list, for `false` the flag is only removed. When the `required` of the object is not a list, nothing is changed.

**Example.** A property schema with `required: true`, as OpenAPI 2 writes it.

**Fix.** Add the name to `required` of the object schema and remove `required` from the property at the source; until then the tool applies this for you, except when `required` of the object is not a list.

### TOA202 `array-without-items`

Default: warning.

An array has no `items` in an OpenAPI 3.0 document, which requires it.

**Example.** `type: array` without `items` in an `openapi: 3.0.x` document.

**Fix.** Add `items` with the element schema at the source, or override `items` of this schema.

### TOA203 `double-array`

Default: warning.

An array's `items` is an array with a boolean `required`: a list declared twice by a decorator.

**Example.** `type: array` with `items: {type: array, required: true}`.

**Fix.** If the field is a flat list, declare it once at the source; until then, override `items` of this schema with the inner `items`.

### TOA204 `format-on-array`

Default: warning.

`format` is on an array without `items` instead of on its elements.

**Example.** `type: array` without `items` and with `format: uuid`.

**Fix.** Move `format` into the elements at the source; until then, override `items` of this schema with the element schema and remove its `format`.

### TOA205 `binary-object`

Default: warning.

`type: object` with `format: binary` instead of a binary string.

**Example.** `type: object` with `format: binary`.

**Fix.** Write `type: string` at the source; until then, override `type` of this schema with `string`.

### TOA206 `contradictory-object-type`

Default: warning.

`type: object` next to `oneOf`/`anyOf` whose branches are all of other types.

**Example.** `type: object` next to a `oneOf` of `string` and `integer`.

**Fix.** Remove `type: object` at the source; until then, remove `type` of this schema with an override.

### TOA207 `example-type-mismatch`

Default: warning.

An `example` whose structure the schema does not allow: an object for an array, or a structure for a scalar and back.

**Example.** A schema `type: array` with `example: {id: 1}`.

**Fix.** Fix the schema or the example at the source; if the example is right, override `type` of this schema.

### TOA208 `example-scalar-type`

Default: info.

An `example` that is a scalar of another type than the scalar schema, such as a string for a number; only the documentation is off.

**Example.** A schema `type: number` with `example: "12.5"`.

**Fix.** Write the example as a number at the source.

### TOA211 `invalid-default`

Default: warning.

A schema's `default` is not of the schema's type; it is ignored.

**Example.** A schema `type: integer` with `default: "ten"`.

**Fix.** Change the default to a value of the schema's type, or remove it; until then the tool removes it for you.

### TOA250 `mixed-type-schema`

Default: warning.

A schema allows several JSON types besides `null` (`type: [string, integer]`); it is generated as `JsonValue`.

**Example.** `type: [string, integer]`.

**Fix.** Give the schema one type at the source, or a Dart type with an override.

### TOA251 `recursive-alias`

Default: warning.

A schema that is not an object, an enum or a union refers to itself (`A: {type: array, items: {$ref: A}}`); the reference is generated as `JsonValue`.

**Example.** `A: {type: array, items: {$ref: '#/components/schemas/A'}}`.

**Fix.** Make the recursive part an object schema at the source.

### TOA252 `allof-property-conflict`

Default: info.

Two `allOf` parts define the same property with different schemas; the later part's is used.

**Example.** Two `allOf` parts that both define `id`, one as a string and one as an integer.

**Fix.** Define each property in one `allOf` part at the source.

### TOA253 `allof-part-ignored`

Default: warning.

An `allOf` part is not an object (a scalar, an enum or a union), so it cannot be merged into a model; it is ignored.

**Example.** An `allOf` part that is `{type: string}` or an enum next to an object part.

**Fix.** Make every `allOf` part an object schema at the source.

### TOA254 `excluded-schema-referenced`

Default: info.

A schema an override excludes is used by a generated type; the use is generated as `JsonValue`. An excluded `allOf` part is the exception: it is merged into the flat model all the same, and this says so. Also reported when an excluded schema has a custom Dart type: the type is used and the exclude has no effect.

**Example.** An override `exclude: true` on a schema that a property of another schema refers to, or on a schema that also has a custom Dart type.

**Fix.** Exclude what uses the schema too, or give the schema a custom Dart type instead of excluding it; when it has both, remove the `exclude` or the custom type.

### TOA255 `oneof-constraints-ignored`

Default: info.

An object with `properties` has a `oneOf` or `anyOf` whose branches only add constraints (`required`, `minProperties`, ...); it is generated as a model and the branches are ignored.

**Example.** An object with `properties` and a `oneOf` whose branches are only `{required: [a]}` and `{required: [b]}`.

**Fix.** Nothing to do; the client does not check the constraints.

### TOA256 `composition-parts-ignored`

Default: warning.

Parts, properties or branches of a schema are ignored because another keyword decides its shape: `allOf` parts or `properties` beside a `oneOf` or `anyOf` union, or the union's branches when the schema is a model made of `allOf` parts or `properties`.

**Example.** A schema with `oneOf: [A, B]` and also `properties`.

**Fix.** Move the properties into the branches, or make the schema a plain union at the source.

## Enums (TOA3xx)

Enum values and their names.

| Code | Slug | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [TOA301](#toa301-duplicate-enum-value) | `duplicate-enum-value` | warning |
| [TOA303](#toa303-nullable-enum-one-of) | `nullable-enum-one-of` | warning |
| [TOA350](#toa350-enum-mixed-values) | `enum-mixed-values` | warning |
| [TOA351](#toa351-enum-varnames-invalid) | `enum-varnames-invalid` | warning |

### TOA301 `duplicate-enum-value`

Default: warning.

An `enum` repeats a value; the repeats are removed.

**Example.** `enum: [a, b, a]`.

**Fix.** Remove the repeated values at the source; until then the tool removes them for you.

### TOA303 `nullable-enum-one-of`

Default: warning.

A nullable enum written as `oneOf` of an enum of only `null` and a `$ref`.

**Example.** `oneOf: [{enum: [null]}, {$ref: '#/components/schemas/Status'}]`.

**Fix.** Write a nullable reference at the source; until then, override this schema as a nullable `$ref`.

### TOA350 `enum-mixed-values`

Default: warning.

An enum mixes values of several JSON types, or has objects or lists among its values; it is generated as `JsonValue`.

**Example.** `enum: [1, "two", true]`.

**Fix.** Give the enum values of one JSON type at the source.

### TOA351 `enum-varnames-invalid`

Default: warning.

`x-enum-varnames` or `x-enum-descriptions` is not a list of strings as long as the enum; it is ignored.

**Example.** An enum of three values with `x-enum-varnames` that lists two names.

**Fix.** Make `x-enum-varnames` a list of strings with one name for each enum value.

| [TOA452](#toa452-discriminator-without-subtypes) | `discriminator-without-subtypes` | info |
| [TOA453](#toa453-union-undiscriminated) | `union-undiscriminated` | warning |
| [TOA454](#toa454-union-variant-duplicate) | `union-variant-duplicate` | info |
| [TOA455](#toa455-union-branch-subsumed) | `union-branch-subsumed` | info |
| [TOA456](#toa456-discriminator-value-duplicate) | `discriminator-value-duplicate` | warning |
| [TOA457](#toa457-discriminator-value-derived) | `discriminator-value-derived` | info |
| [TOA458](#toa458-union-json-type-shadowed) | `union-json-type-shadowed` | info |

### TOA401 `discriminator-not-required`

Default: info.

The discriminator property is not required in a variant.

**Example.** A union with `discriminator.propertyName: kind` whose variants do not list `kind` in `required`.

**Fix.** Add the discriminator property to `required` of each variant at the source.

### TOA402 `discriminator-mapping-unresolved`

Default: error.

A `discriminator.mapping` value points to a schema that does not exist.

**Example.** `mapping: {cat: '#/components/schemas/Kat'}` when there is no `Kat` schema.

**Fix.** Point the mapping at an existing schema at the source; until then, override the mapping of this discriminator.

### TOA450 `discriminator-value-missing`

Default: warning.

A variant of a union with a discriminator is written inline, so no discriminator value selects it.

**Example.** A union with a discriminator whose variant is an inline object, not a `$ref`.

**Fix.** Make the variant a component schema and `$ref` it.

### TOA451 `discriminator-mapping-not-variant`

Default: info.

A `discriminator.mapping` value, or the `defaultMapping`, names a schema that is not a variant of the union; it is ignored. A value that maps to the base schema itself, which is generated as the union of its subtypes, is decoded as the unknown variant with its JSON kept.

**Example.** A `mapping` value that names a schema the union's `oneOf` does not list, or one that maps to the base schema itself.

**Fix.** Map the value to a variant of the union, or to a schema that extends the base.

### TOA452 `discriminator-without-subtypes`

Default: info.

A `discriminator` sits on a schema that is neither a `oneOf`/`anyOf` union nor a base other schemas extend with `allOf`: nothing can be picked by it, so the schema is generated as a model.

**Example.** A schema with a `discriminator` that no other schema extends with `allOf` and that is not a union.

**Fix.** Extend the schema with `allOf` in its subtypes, or list them in a `oneOf`.

### TOA453 `union-undiscriminated`

Default: warning.

A `oneOf` or `anyOf` without a discriminator has variants of the same JSON type, or a variant that can hold several (a nested union without a discriminator), so a value cannot be told apart: the union keeps it as `JsonValue` in one variant (`PetJson`), or, when no variant has a JSON type of its own, is `JsonValue` itself. An override `union: structural` (or the config key `union`) generates a union that tries the variants; a discriminator at the source is better.

**Example.** `oneOf: [{$ref: Cat}, {$ref: Dog}]`, both objects, with no discriminator.

**Fix.** Add a discriminator at the source, or generate a union that tries the variants with `union: structural` (an override of the schema, or the config key for every such union).

### TOA454 `union-variant-duplicate`

Default: info.

Two variants of a union have the same Dart type; the later one is dropped, since a value could not be told apart between them.

**Example.** A `oneOf` with two inline `{type: string}` branches.

**Fix.** Remove the duplicate variant at the source.

### TOA455 `union-branch-subsumed`

Default: info.

A branch of a `oneOf` or `anyOf` without a discriminator is an enum or a `const` of a primitive type (`string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`) while another branch is that type with no constraint: the values of the first are values of the second, so the branch is dropped and, when one branch remains, the union is that type (Stripe's `anyOf: [string, {enum: ['']}]`). An integer enum next to a plain `number` is dropped too; a number enum next to an `integer` is not.

The other branch counts as plain when it has no `enum`, `const`, `format`, `pattern` or keyword the rule does not model (`if`, `not`, `dependentSchemas`, ...), and every enum value meets its length and range constraints (`multipleOf` on the exact decimal numbers). From OpenAPI 3.1 the keywords next to the `$ref` of a branch are the branch's own and are held to the same rule; 3.0 ignores them. The values of a dropped branch stay in the documentation of the field ("Known values") when the union is a union class or collapses; a union that stays `JsonValue` lists none.

For a `oneOf` the collapse is looser than the spec: a value both branches take (`''` for `oneOf: [string, {const: ''}]`) is rejected by the `oneOf` and accepted by the type. This is accepted on purpose: the idiom is common (Stripe), its authors mean "any of these", and the client does not validate.

**Example.** `anyOf: [{type: string}, {enum: ['']}]`.

**Fix.** Remove the enum branch at the source, or leave it for the documentation.

### TOA456 `discriminator-value-duplicate`

Default: warning.

Two variants of a union with a discriminator are selected by the same value (a `const` of the property, a mapping entry or the implicit name): the earlier variant decodes it, and the later one is never picked by that value.

**Example.** Two variants that both fix `kind` to `"circle"`, or a mapping that sends one value to two schemas.

**Fix.** Give each variant its own discriminator value, in the mapping or in the `const` of the property.

### TOA457 `discriminator-value-derived`

Default: info.

A `$ref` variant that the discriminator's `mapping` does not name fixes the discriminator property to one value (a `const` or a one-value `enum`, also through a `$ref` or an `allOf` part) that is not its component name: that value selects it, not the name OpenAPI implies (OpenAI's tool unions). An explicit `mapping` entry always wins.

**Example.** A variant `ToolCall` without a mapping entry whose `type` property is `const: function`.

**Fix.** Add the value to the `mapping` to say so, or map the component name if the payloads carry it.

### TOA458 `union-json-type-shadowed`

Default: info.

A non-object variant of a union with a discriminator has the JSON type of an earlier variant (a string enum next to a plain string): a value of that type is decoded as the earlier variant, since a value that is not an object has no discriminator property to tell them apart, so this variant is never produced when decoding.

**Example.** A union with a discriminator that has `{type: string}` and, after it, a string enum.

**Fix.** Remove the variant at the source, or give the earlier variant a type that does not take every value of that JSON type.

## Paths, naming and operations (TOA5xx)

Operation ids, parameters, groups and Dart names.

| Code | Slug | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |

| [TOA566](#toa566-operation-servers-ignored) | `operation-servers-ignored` | warning |

### TOA501 `missing-path-parameter`

Default: warning.

A variable of the path template has no path parameter; one is added.

**Example.** The path `/products/{id}` on an operation that declares no `id` parameter.

**Fix.** Declare each at the source as a parameter with `in: path`, `required: true` and `schema: {type: string}`; until then the tool adds it for you.

### TOA502 `path-parameter-not-in-template`

Default: error.

A path parameter is not a variable of the path template, or is one in another case.

**Example.** A path parameter `userId` on the path `/users/{id}`.

**Fix.** Make the parameter name and the template variable the same at the source; until then, override the name of this parameter.

### TOA503 `missing-operation-id`

Default: info.

An operation has no `operationId`.

**Example.** A `get:` operation without `operationId`.

**Fix.** Add an `operationId` at the source, or override the method name of this operation.

### TOA504 `duplicate-operation-id`

Default: error.

Two operations share an `operationId`.

**Example.** Two operations with `operationId: getPets`.

**Fix.** Give each operation its own `operationId` at the source. To generate anyway, lower this code in the client's `severity` and pin the second method's name with an override.

### TOA550 `name-reserved`

Default: info.

A name from the spec is a Dart reserved word or a name Dart already has (`class`, `List`); the generated name gets a suffix.

**Example.** A schema named `List` or a property named `class`.

**Fix.** Rename it at the source if the suffix is unwelcome, or name it with an override.

### TOA551 `name-collision`

Default: info.

Two generated declarations, members or arguments would have the same name; the later one (by spec location) gets a suffix.

**Example.** Schemas `PetList` and `pet_list`, which both become `PetList`.

**Fix.** Rename the other type, or rename this one.

### TOA552 `name-unrepresentable`

Default: warning.

A name from the spec has no ASCII letter or digit, so no Dart name can be made from it; a generic name is used.

**Example.** A schema named `日本語`.

**Fix.** Rename the schema at the source, or name its type with an override.

### TOA553 `operation-multiple-tags`

Default: info.

An operation has several tags; it is generated once, in the group of its first tag.

**Example.** An operation with `tags: [pets, store]`.

**Fix.** Keep one tag at the source, or name the group with an override `group`.

### TOA554 `operation-untagged`

Default: info.

An operation has no tag; it is generated in the default group.

**Example.** An operation with no `tags`.

**Fix.** Tag the operations at the source, or set `group_by` to `path` or `single` in the config.

### TOA555 `tags-merged`

Default: info.

Two tags differ only in case or separators, so they give one group.

**Example.** Tags `pet-store` and `PetStore`.

**Fix.** Write the tag the same way everywhere at the source.

### TOA556 `path-variable-unbound`

Default: error.

A variable of the path template has no path parameter with its exact name (`{ID}` with a parameter `id`); the operation is not generated.

**Example.** The path `/users/{ID}` with a parameter named `id`.

**Fix.** Declare a path parameter with the exact name of the variable at the source.

### TOA557 `filter-matches-nothing`

Default: warning.

A tag, `operationId` or path pattern of the config's `include` or `exclude` matches no operation of the spec.

**Example.** `include: {tags: [petz]}` in the config when the spec has the tag `pets`.

**Fix.** Fix the pattern, or remove it from the config.

### TOA558 `filter-conflict`

Default: info.

The config lists the same tag, `operationId` or path pattern in both `include` and `exclude`; `exclude` wins.

**Example.** The tag `internal` in both `include` and `exclude` of one client.

**Fix.** Remove it from one of the filters.

### TOA559 `name-lossy`

Default: info.

A name from the spec lost characters when it became a Dart name (`Größe` became `grE`: letters outside ASCII are dropped). Changes of case and separators (`my_thing`, `X-Request-ID`) are not reported.

**Example.** A property named `Größe`, which becomes `grE` because letters outside ASCII are dropped.

**Fix.** Name it explicitly to keep the meaning: the text of the diagnostic ends with an `Override:` snippet. For a client name, set `naming.client` in the config.

### TOA560 `override-name-invalid`

Default: warning.

An override `name` (of a schema, property, operation, parameter) or `group` is not a valid Dart name for what it names (`my thing`, `1x`, `_private`), or loses characters when it is made one; the name made from it is used, or the override is ignored when nothing is left. A `group` that differs from UpperCamelCase only by case or separators (`pet-store`) is not reported: it is used as `PetStore`.

**Example.** An override `name: my thing` or `name: 1x`.

**Fix.** Give the override a valid Dart name of the right kind, or remove it.

### TOA563 `client-empty`

Default: warning.

No operation of a client is generated: all are filtered out, all are written as a `$ref` (TOA107), all have an unbound path variable (TOA556), all are event streams the client cannot express (TOA654) or all are left out by overrides. The message says why.

**Example.** A client whose `include` filter leaves no operation.

**Fix.** Fix the filters of the client, or the spec; the message says why nothing is generated.

### TOA564 `parameter-style-invalid`

Default: warning.

A parameter's `style` is not allowed for its `in` (path takes `simple`, `label` or `matrix`; query `form`, `spaceDelimited`, `pipeDelimited` or `deepObject`; header `simple`; cookie `form` or `cookie`), or the `style` of the `encoding` of a form property is not one a query takes, so the default style is used.

**Example.** A query parameter with `style: simple`, or a path parameter with `style: form`.

**Fix.** Use one of the styles the parameter's location allows at the source.

### TOA565 `querystring-not-generated`

Default: warning.

A parameter is `in: querystring` (OpenAPI 3.2), which the client cannot send yet: the parameter is not generated.

**Example.** A parameter with `in: querystring`.

**Fix.** Describe the query string as query parameters at the source.

### TOA566 `operation-servers-ignored`

Default: warning.

A path item or an operation has its own `servers`; the client sends every request to the base URL of the user's transport.

**Example.** An operation with its own `servers: [{url: https://upload.example.com}]`.

**Fix.** Send these requests through a transport with that base URL, or move the servers to the document.

### TOA567 `callbacks-not-generated`

Default: info.

An operation has `callbacks`, or the document has `webhooks`: requests the server makes, which the client does not generate.

**Example.** An operation with `callbacks:` or a document with `webhooks:`.

**Fix.** Nothing to do; the client sends requests and does not receive them.

### TOA568 `security-scheme-unknown`

Default: warning.

A security requirement names a scheme that `components.securitySchemes` does not have (or defines without a valid type), or is not an object (a string, `null`; also TOA111), or the `security` field is not a list (also TOA111): the alternative is left out of the operation's metadata when another one can be described, else it stays with a scheme of the kind unknown.

**Example.** `security: [{apiKeyAuth: []}]` when `components.securitySchemes` has no `apiKeyAuth`.

**Fix.** Write the requirement as an object that names a scheme the document defines, at the source.

### TOA569 `locked-name-taken`

Default: warning.

`typed_openapi.lock` keeps a name for a type or a method, but an override's name or a custom type took it first, or the kept name is not a usable Dart name for what it names (a hand-edited lock): it is named anew.

**Example.** `typed_openapi.lock` keeps the name `Pet`, and an override now names another type `Pet`; or a lock edited by hand keeps the name `my pet`.

**Fix.** Rename the override or the custom type, or accept the new name; run `generate --fresh-names` to write new names to the lock.

### TOA570 `locked-name-kept`

Default: info.

`typed_openapi.lock` keeps the name of a type or a method that a run without the lock would name otherwise.

**Example.** A schema renamed in the spec whose type keeps the name `typed_openapi.lock` recorded.

**Fix.** Run `generate --fresh-names` to take the new names.

### TOA571 `locked-name-released`

Default: info.

`typed_openapi.lock` keeps a name for a type the spec no longer declares: the name is free again.

**Example.** A schema removed from the spec whose name the lock still keeps.

**Fix.** Nothing to do; the next `generate` drops it from the lock.

Bodies, responses, defaults and Server-Sent Events.

| [TOA655](#toa655-multipart-not-object) | `multipart-not-object` | warning |

| [TOA657](#toa657-response-status-invalid) | `response-status-invalid` | warning |
| [TOA658](#toa658-response-status-not-generated) | `response-status-not-generated` | info |
| [TOA659](#toa659-encoding-key-unknown) | `encoding-key-unknown` | warning |
| [TOA660](#toa660-default-value-invalid) | `default-value-invalid` | warning |
| [TOA661](#toa661-part-media-type-chosen) | `part-media-type-chosen` | info |
| [TOA662](#toa662-part-media-type-not-json) | `part-media-type-not-json` | warning |
| [TOA663](#toa663-event-stream-method-added) | `event-stream-method-added` | info |
| [TOA664](#toa664-event-data-array-items) | `event-data-array-items` | info |
| [TOA665](#toa665-event-stream-reconnect-off) | `event-stream-reconnect-off` | info |
| [TOA666](#toa666-event-item-schema-unread) | `event-item-schema-unread` | warning |
| [TOA667](#toa667-event-name-duplicate) | `event-name-duplicate` | warning |
| [TOA668](#toa668-event-name-unrepresentable) | `event-name-unrepresentable` | info |
| [TOA669](#toa669-sse-override-not-applied) | `sse-override-not-applied` | warning |
| [TOA670](#toa670-event-name-unreachable) | `event-name-unreachable` | warning |
| [TOA671](#toa671-event-stream-error-as-text) | `event-stream-error-as-text` | info |

### TOA601 `wildcard-media-type`

Default: warning.

`*/*` is used as a media type.

**Example.** A response with the media type `*/*`.

**Fix.** Declare the actual media type (usually `application/json`) at the source, or override the content type here.

### TOA650 `media-type-as-bytes`

Default: info.

A request or response body has a media type that is not JSON, a form, `multipart/form-data`, `text/*` or `text/event-stream` (or is a form or multipart response): it is sent or read as bytes and its schema is not used.

**Example.** A response in `application/pdf`, or a request body in `application/xml`.

**Fix.** Use a JSON media type at the source if the schema matters.

### TOA651 `media-types-dropped`

Default: info.

A request body, a response or a parameter offers several media types; the client uses one and the message names the ones it drops.

**Example.** A request body that offers both `application/json` and `application/xml`.

**Fix.** Offer one media type at the source if the client should use another; for `sse.method: only`, remove it to keep the body in a method too.

### TOA652 `default-error-schema-missing`

Default: warning.

`errors.default_schema` names a key that is not in `components.schemas`; the setting is ignored.

**Example.** `errors: {default_schema: ApiError}` in the config when `components.schemas` has no `ApiError`.

**Fix.** Name a key of `components.schemas`, or remove the setting.

### TOA653 `success-undocumented`

Default: warning.

An operation documents no 2xx response: any 2xx is a success whose value is the body as `JsonValue`.

**Example.** An operation whose `responses` has only `404` and `500`.

**Fix.** Document the success response at the source.

### TOA654 `event-stream-not-generated`

Default: warning.

An event-stream operation has a shape the client cannot express: its event-stream successes have different event types, or another success has a body that is not an event stream. The operation is not generated when some of its successes are only a stream; when each stream offers a body too, only the event-stream method is left out and the method that returns the body is generated. Also reported when an `sse` override of the event types does not reach a shared `$ref`'d response, so the event types still differ.

**Example.** An operation whose `200` is `text/event-stream` and whose `201` is `application/json` only; or two event-stream successes with different `itemSchema`s.

**Fix.** Offer `text/event-stream` on every success with a body and give the event-stream successes one event type; for a shared `$ref`'d response, override the schema it uses by its component name, or write the response in the operation.

### TOA655 `multipart-not-object`

Default: warning.

The schema of a multipart body is not an object with properties (a union, an `allOf`, a map): there is no class of parts, the body is the schema's type, each property of its JSON is a part, and a binary string is sent as base64 text, not as a file.

**Example.** A `multipart/form-data` body whose schema is a `oneOf` or a map.

**Fix.** Describe the body as an object with a property for each part at the source.

### TOA656 `encoding-headers-ignored`

Default: info.

An `encoding` entry of a multipart part or of a form property has `headers`, which the client does not send.

**Example.** An `encoding` entry of a multipart part with `headers: {X-Rate: ...}`.

**Fix.** Send the headers another way, or remove them at the source.

### TOA657 `response-status-invalid`

Default: warning.

A key of an operation's `responses` is not an HTTP status: OpenAPI allows a code from 100 to 599, a range (`1XX` to `5XX`, in either case) and `default`. The response is not generated, so a key written by a tool or by hand can never reach a name or an expression of the client. A key that repeats another one in a different case (`2xx` and `2XX`) is reported the same way.

**Example.** A `responses` key `"20"` or `"success"`.

**Fix.** Rename or remove the key at the source.

### TOA658 `response-status-not-generated`

Default: info.

A response documents a 1xx or 3xx status. The client has no result for them (Dio follows redirects and the interim statuses are not responses), so the response is not generated; at run time the status is an undocumented one, or handled by the `default` response when the operation has one.

**Example.** A `responses` key `301` or `100`.

**Fix.** Nothing to do; the status is handled as undocumented or by the `default` response.

### TOA659 `encoding-key-unknown`

Default: warning.

An `encoding` key of a form or multipart body names no property of the body's schema (a misspelled name, a property the schema does not have): the entry is ignored.

**Example.** An `encoding` entry `avatr` when the body's schema has the property `avatar`.

**Fix.** Use the name of a property of the schema, or remove the entry.

### TOA660 `default-value-invalid`

Default: warning.

The `default` of a parameter does not match the parameter's `enum` or `format` (`default: other` for `enum: [a, b]`, a `format: date` default that is not a date): it is not documented as the default.

**Example.** A parameter with `enum: [a, b]` and `default: other`.

**Fix.** Use a default that fits the schema at the source.

### TOA661 `part-media-type-chosen`

Default: info.

The `contentType` of an `encoding` entry of a multipart part is a list (`image/png, image/jpeg`), a wildcard (`image/*`) or no media type: the part is sent with one concrete type, the file's own when it has one, else the first concrete type of the list, else `application/octet-stream` for a file and no media type for text.

**Example.** A multipart part with `encoding.contentType: image/png, image/jpeg`.

**Fix.** Name one concrete media type in the encoding at the source.

### TOA662 `part-media-type-not-json`

Default: warning.

An object part of a multipart body has a `contentType` that is not JSON (`application/xml`). The client writes JSON only, so the part is a `String` the caller supplies, sent with that media type.

**Example.** A multipart object part with `encoding.contentType: application/xml`.

**Fix.** Write the value in that format yourself and pass the text, or describe the part as a string at the source.

### TOA663 `event-stream-method-added`

Default: info.

A success of an operation offers JSON (or another body) and `text/event-stream`: the operation gets a second method, named with `naming.stream_suffix`, that returns the events.

**Example.** An operation whose `200` offers `application/json` and `text/event-stream`.

**Fix.** Nothing to do; set `naming.stream_suffix` in the config to name the second method otherwise.

### TOA664 `event-data-array-items`

Default: info.

The `schema` of an event stream is an array: each event's data is taken to be one item, as code-first frameworks write it.

**Example.** A `text/event-stream` response whose `schema` is `{type: array, items: {$ref: Message}}`.

**Fix.** Describe one event at the source (`itemSchema` in OpenAPI 3.2).

### TOA665 `event-stream-reconnect-off`

Default: info.

`sse.reconnect` in the config asks event streams to reconnect, but it applies to GET only: an event-stream operation that is not GET does not reconnect, since repeating the request may not be safe, unless its own `sse.reconnect` override enables it. Reported once per such operation, and only when the config asks.

**Example.** `sse: {reconnect: true}` in the config and a `POST` operation that returns an event stream.

**Fix.** Enable `sse.reconnect` for this operation with an override if the request can be repeated.

### TOA666 `event-item-schema-unread`

Default: warning.

The `itemSchema` of an event stream does not say what the data of an event is (no `data` property, or one that is neither text nor JSON with a `contentSchema`): the data is read as text.

**Example.** An `itemSchema` whose `data` property is an object without `contentMediaType`.

**Fix.** Give `data` `contentMediaType: application/json` and a `contentSchema` at the source.

### TOA667 `event-name-duplicate`

Default: warning.

Two branches of an `itemSchema` union fix the same event name: the later one is left out.

**Example.** Two branches of an `itemSchema` `oneOf` that both fix `event` to `"update"`.

**Fix.** Give each event its own name at the source.

### TOA668 `event-name-unrepresentable`

Default: info.

An event name has no ASCII letter or digit (`""`, `*/`), so its variant is named by its place (`ChatEventEvent2`).

**Example.** An event named `*/`.

**Fix.** Name the event with letters at the source.

### TOA669 `sse-override-not-applied`

Default: warning.

A part of the `sse` override of an operation does not apply: `data` or `events` find no `text/event-stream` 2xx response written in the operation (a `$ref`'d one is shared), the operation has no event stream for `reconnect`, `method` or `unknown`, `unknown` has no events by name to apply to, or an event's data cannot be read. The message names the part; the rest of `sse` applies.

**Example.** An `sse: {data: Message}` override on an operation whose event stream response is a shared `$ref`.

**Fix.** Remove the part the message names, or write the response in the operation; a shared response is overridden through the schema it uses, by its component name.

### TOA670 `event-name-unreachable`

Default: warning.

An event name that no `event:` line can carry: an empty one (the wire reads it as `message`) or one with a line break. Its variant could never be selected, so it is left out.

**Example.** An event fixed to `""` or to a name with a line break.

**Fix.** Give the event a name that fits on an `event:` line at the source.

### TOA671 `event-stream-error-as-text`

Default: info.

A `text/event-stream` response with an error status (or `default`) of an operation whose method does not return events: its body is read as text, like any other error body that is not JSON.

**Example.** A `500` response in `text/event-stream` on an operation that returns JSON.

**Fix.** Use a JSON media type for errors at the source if the schema matters.

## Fixes, overrides, baseline and generate (TOA8xx)

Applying fixes and overrides, baselines, and writing the output.

### TOA800 `fix-not-applied`

Default: warning.

A normalizer fix or an override was not applied: its file cannot be read, its target is gone, the spec kept changing after the last pass, or the change would have no effect in the spec's dialect.

**Example.** A fix that still changes the spec after the third pass, or an override that would sit beside a `$ref` in an `openapi: 3.0.x` document.

**Fix.** Read the message; usually override the referenced schema by name, or make the change at the source.

### TOA801 `overrides-not-found`

Default: error (fixed).

The overrides file a client names does not exist.

**Example.** `overrides: overrides.yaml` in the config when the file is not there.

**Fix.** Create the file, or fix `overrides` of this client in the config.

### TOA802 `invalid-override`

Default: error (fixed).

The overrides file cannot be read, or an override has a value of the wrong type, or a field that cannot be set where it is (on a schema that is a reference, or together with `nullable` on a schema that is nullable through `anyOf` or `oneOf`); the value is ignored.

**Example.** An overrides file that is a list, an override with `exclude: "yes"`, or a field other than `nullable` on a schema that is a `$ref`.

**Fix.** Point `overrides` of this client at the overrides file itself, give each field the type the message names, and override `nullable` alone, or the schema by its name, where other fields cannot be set.

### TOA803 `unknown-override-key`

Default: error (fixed).

An override has a key this tool does not know, such as a misspelled field; it is ignored.

**Example.** An override with `nme: Pet`.

**Fix.** Fix the spelling; the message names the closest known key (`Did you mean "name"?`) when one is within edit distance 2, then lists the allowed keys.

### TOA804 `override-target-not-found`

Default: warning.

An override names an operation, a schema, a property, a parameter or a response the spec does not have; it is not applied.

**Example.** An override for the operation `getPetz` when the spec has `getPets`.

**Fix.** Remove the override, or fix its address.

### TOA805 `override-target-ambiguous`

Default: error.

An override's address names more than one node, such as an `operationId` two operations share; it is not applied.

**Example.** An override for `operationId: list` that two operations share, or for a parameter `id` found in the path and the query.

**Fix.** For an `operationId` two operations share, address the operation as `METHOD /path`; for parameters with one name, write the key as `in:name`; for a response with several media types, add `contentType` to the override.

### TOA806 `override-conflict`

Default: error.

Two overrides change the same node; neither is applied.

**Example.** Two override entries for `getPets`, one by `operationId` and one by `GET /pets`.

**Fix.** Merge them into one override.

### TOA807 `override-unchanged`

Default: info.

An override sets a value the spec already has, or a generation field has no effect (a `name` or `exhaustive` on an alias, a `name` on a schema that only a multipart body uses); it can be removed.

**Example.** An override that sets `nullable: true` on a schema that is already nullable.

**Fix.** Remove the override.

### TOA808 `override-shared-target`

Default: info.

An override addressed through an operation changes a node other operations may share: a path-level parameter, a `$ref`'d component or a node in another file.

**Example.** A parameter override that changes a parameter defined once at the path level for every operation.

**Fix.** Nothing to do if every operation should change; otherwise override each operation's own parameter.

### TOA809 `override-nullability-dropped`

Default: info.

An override removes the `type` of a nullable 3.1 schema, so the schema is no longer nullable: nullability is the `null` in that `type`.

**Example.** An override `type: null` on a schema with `type: [string, "null"]`.

**Fix.** Nothing to do if the schema should stop being nullable; remove the override if it should stay nullable.

### TOA810 `override-operation-not-generated`

Default: warning.

An override addresses an operation that the client's `include` or `exclude` filter leaves out, so the entry and the overrides of its parameters, body and responses change nothing in the generated client. An entry with its own `exclude: true` is not reported.

**Example.** The entry `GET /social-networks/facebook/auth-links` in the overrides file while `include` of the client does not list that operation.

**Fix.** Remove the entry, or change `include` or `exclude` so that the operation is generated.

### TOA820 `baseline-not-found`

Default: error (fixed).

The baseline file a client names does not exist.

**Example.** `baseline: baseline.yaml` in the config when the file is not there.

**Fix.** Write it with `typed_openapi baseline create`, or fix `baseline` of this client in the config.

### TOA821 `invalid-baseline`

Default: error (fixed).

The baseline file cannot be read, or an entry is malformed and is ignored.

**Example.** A baseline file that is not YAML, has `version: 2`, or has an entry without a `code`.

**Fix.** Point `baseline` of this client at the baseline file itself, or recreate it with `typed_openapi baseline create`.

### TOA822 `baseline-entry-stale`

Default: warning.

A baseline entry accepts more diagnostics than the check finds: the problem was fixed, and `baseline prune` can remove the entry.

**Example.** A baseline entry for a problem the spec no longer has.

**Fix.** Run `typed_openapi baseline prune`.

### TOA823 `baseline-not-written`

Default: error (fixed).

The baseline file cannot be written.

**Example.** `baseline create` in a directory that cannot be written.

**Fix.** Make the baseline file's location writable.

### TOA830 `output-not-owned`

Default: error (fixed).

`generate` refuses a client's output directory, which it would replace: it holds a `pubspec.yaml`, is the `lib` directory of a package, holds a symbolic link or an input of the run, or holds a file it did not write or that changed since it wrote it (a file the manifest does not list or whose hash differs, or any file when there is no manifest); the message names the files, and `--force` replaces them, but never a package, a link or an input. Nothing is written for the client.

**Example.** An output directory that holds a `pubspec.yaml`, or a hand-written file next to the generated ones.

**Fix.** Move the hand-written files out, point `output` at a directory the generator owns, or run `generate --force` to replace files (never a package, a link or an input).

### TOA831 `output-not-written`

Default: error (fixed).

`generate` cannot write a client's output directory, or another run holds its lock (`.<output>.typed_openapi.lock` next to the output; a lock of a process that is gone is taken over, and `--break-lock` takes over one whose owner cannot be told).

**Example.** An output directory on a read-only file system, or a second `generate` running on the same output.

**Fix.** Check whether another `generate` runs on this output; delete the lock file or use `--break-lock` only when its owner is gone.

### TOA832 `output-recovered`

Default: info (fixed).

An earlier `generate` was killed while it replaced the output directory and left the previous tree or a half-built one in sibling directories named `.<output>.typed_openapi-*`. The run put the previous output back, when the output was missing, and removed the leftovers. Also reported when a run takes over the lock of a process that is gone, or breaks a lock whose owner cannot be told with `--break-lock`.

**Example.** A `generate` that was killed halfway through replacing the output.

**Fix.** Nothing to do after a recovery: the output is back as it was before the killed run. After a lock take-over, check that no other `generate` still runs on this output.

### TOA833 `output-file-replaced`

Default: info (fixed).

`generate --force` overwrote or deleted a file that it did not write or that changed since it wrote it; one report for each file.

**Example.** `generate --force` over a hand-edited generated file.

**Fix.** Nothing to do; keep hand-written code outside the output directory.

### TOA834 `api-lock-differs`

Default: error (fixed).

`generate --locked` found that a client's API differs from its snapshot in `typed_openapi.lock`, or that the lock has no snapshot of it, or one of a client the config no longer declares. The client is not written and the lock is not changed.

**Example.** `generate --locked` in CI after the spec changed a type without a committed lock.

**Fix.** Run `generate` without `--locked` and commit the lock; `typed_openapi diff` lists the changes.

### TOA835 `api-lock-unusable`

Default: error (fixed).

`typed_openapi.lock` cannot be read, is not a lock of version 1, or cannot be written. A run that cannot read it writes no client.

**Example.** A `typed_openapi.lock` with unresolved merge conflict markers.

**Fix.** Resolve the merge conflict in the file, or delete it to start from the current API.

## Config (TOA9xx)

Reading `typed_openapi.yaml`.

| Code | Slug | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [TOA901](#toa901-config-not-found) | `config-not-found` | error (config) |
| [TOA902](#toa902-config-invalid) | `config-invalid` | error (config) |
| [TOA903](#toa903-config-unknown-key) | `config-unknown-key` | warning (config) |
| [TOA904](#toa904-output-overlap) | `output-overlap` | error (config) |

### TOA901 `config-not-found`

Default: error (config).

The configuration file does not exist.

**Example.** `--config` naming a file that is not there, or no `typed_openapi.yaml` in the working directory.

**Fix.** Create `typed_openapi.yaml`, or pass its path with `--config`.

### TOA902 `config-invalid`

Default: error (config).

The configuration file is malformed or has an invalid value.

**Example.** A `typed_openapi.yaml` that is a list, a client without `input`, or `group_by: tags`.

**Fix.** Pass the path of `typed_openapi.yaml` itself with `--config`, and fix the value the message names.

### TOA903 `config-unknown-key`

Default: warning (config).

The configuration file has a key this tool does not know.

**Example.** A config with `clients.shop.outptu:`.

**Fix.** Fix the spelling; the message lists the allowed keys at that place (`Allowed keys here: ...`).

### TOA904 `output-overlap`

Default: error (config).

Two clients write to the same or nested output directories.

**Example.** Two clients whose `output` is `lib/api` and `lib/api/shop`.

**Fix.** Give each client its own output directory.

## Where codes are reported

| Stage | Codes | Reported by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reading files | TOA001-TOA022 | `check`, `generate`, `baseline` |
| Normalizer rules | TOA106, TOA201-TOA208, TOA211, TOA301, TOA303, TOA401, TOA402, TOA501-TOA504, TOA601 | one of the normalizer rules, see [Presets and rules](presets_and_rules.md) |
| Mapping to Dart | the other TOA2xx-TOA6xx | the IR builder while it names and types the client |
| Overrides | TOA560, TOA800-TOA810 | the overrides file, see [Overrides](overrides.md) |
| Baseline | TOA820-TOA823 | see [Baseline](baseline.md) |
| Generate | TOA830-TOA835 | see [Generated output](generate_output.md) and [the API lock](cli.md#the-api-lock) |
| Config | TOA901-TOA904 | see [Configuration](configuration.md) |
